from.place: General cohomological continuity used after constructing the punctured inverse system: sections on quasi-compact opens are represented and identified at a finite stage.

title: Sections of a sheaf system on a spectral inverse limit descend to a finite stage
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set. Let $X_i$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space], and let $f_{ij}:X_j\to X_i$ for $i\le j$ be continuous maps such that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact, $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ij}\circ f_{jk}=f_{ik}$. Let $X$ be their inverse limit in topological spaces, with projections $p_i:X\to X_i$: its points are the compatible tuples, and its topology is the coarsest making every $p_i$ continuous. For every $i$ let $F_i$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $X_i$, with morphisms $\alpha_{ij}:F_i\to(f_{ij})_*F_j$ satisfying $\alpha_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha_{ik}=(f_{ij})_*\alpha_{jk}\circ\alpha_{ij}$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Put $F=\varinjlim_i p_i^{-1}F_i$ in abelian sheaves on $X$, using the pullbacks of the adjoints $f_{ij}^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ as transition maps [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every $i$ and every quasi-compact open $U_i\subseteq X_i$, the canonical map induced by pullback of sections and the colimit coprojections is an isomorphism of abelian groups: $$\varinjlim_{j\ge i} F_j(f_{ij}^{-1}U_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(p_i^{-1}U_i).$$ The transition homomorphism from index $j$ to $k\ge j$ on the left is the component of $\alpha_{jk}$ over $f_{ij}^{-1}U_i$, with $f_{jk}^{-1}f_{ij}^{-1}U_i=f_{ik}^{-1}U_i$.

proof.text: First pass between abelian sheaves and their underlying sheaves of sets. For any directed diagram of abelian sheaves $A_j$, put $P(V)=\varinjlim_j A_j(V)$ in abelian groups. The restriction maps are induced by those of the $A_j$. The universal properties of the group colimit and of sheafification give $\operatorname{Hom}(P^\#,B)=\varprojlim_j\operatorname{Hom}(A_j,B)$ for every abelian sheaf $B$, so $P^\#$ is the abelian-sheaf colimit. By [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups] and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], the underlying set of each $P(V)$ is the set colimit (both have representatives with equality at a common later stage). By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], $|P^\#|$ is the set sheafification of $|P|$, hence the set-sheaf colimit by the same universal-property calculation. Likewise the presheaf inverse image in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] is a directed colimit over neighbourhood opens; the same two representative descriptions and the same sheafification lemma show that its abelian inverse image has as underlying sheaf the set inverse image, including its section unit. Thus the cited set-sheaf results below apply to the underlying sets of the abelian sheaves without changing the canonical maps.

source.place: Tag 0A33, label lemma-descend-opens, proof: algebraic-structure specialization, with Sites section-sheaves-algebraic-structures

proof.text: Put $U=p_i^{-1}U_i$, $U_j=f_{ij}^{-1}U_i$ for $j\ge i$, and $G_j=p_j^{-1}F_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-directed-limit-spectral], $X$ is spectral and $U$ is quasi-compact open. Any open covering of $U$ refines to a covering by quasi-compact basis opens contained in its members; choose a finite subcover by quasi-compactness. Their pairwise intersections are quasi-compact by [def-weil-spectral-space]. This verifies precisely hypothesis (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-directed-colimit-sections]. Apply that node to the underlying set diagram of the $G_j$ and its colimit (Step 1) to obtain $F(U)=\varinjlim_{j\ge i}G_j(U)$. Restricting to $j\ge i$ loses no cocone data: for any index $a$ choose $b\ge a,i$ and use the map at $b$ after the transition from $a$; two choices agree at a common upper index. All maps are homomorphisms, so this bijection of underlying sets is an isomorphism of groups.

source.place: Tag 0A33, label lemma-descend-opens, proof: first display; Sheaves lemma-directed-colimits-sections and Topology lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces

proof.text: For each $j\ge i$, the open $U_j$ is quasi-compact by the spectrality of $f_{ij}$, and $U=p_j^{-1}U_j$ by $f_{ij}p_j=p_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-pullback-sections] to the underlying set sheaf of $F_j$ and $U_j$. With $H_{j,k}=(f_{jk}^{-1}F_j)(U_k)$ for $k\ge j$, its conclusion gives $G_j(U)=\varinjlim_{k\ge j}H_{j,k}$, using the pullback units and canonical composition isomorphisms specified in that node. Step 1 identifies these with the abelian inverse images. The units and composition identifications are additive (the latter are the canonical identifications of the same left adjoints), so this is also a group isomorphism. These identifications are natural in $F_j$: a sheaf morphism commutes with the unit and with each composition identification, as is seen by precomposing with the section unit in the inverse-image adjunction. Therefore the outer transitions in Step 2 are exactly pullback followed by the coefficient maps adjoint to $\alpha_{jj'}$.

source.place: Tag 0A33, label lemma-descend-opens, proof: last display; application of lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit

proof.text: Write $\beta_{jk}:f_{jk}^{-1}F_j\to F_k$ for the adjoint of $\alpha_{jk}$, so $\beta_{jj}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta_{jl}=\beta_{kl}\circ f_{kl}^{-1}\beta_{jk}$ under the canonical composition identification. Set $B_k=F_k(U_k)$ and $L=\varinjlim_{k\ge i}B_k$, with its maps $b_k$. Define $q_{j,k}:H_{j,k}\to L$ by $q_{j,k}=b_k\circ\beta_{jk,U_k}$. For $l\ge k$, applying the pullback unit and then $\beta_{jl}$ equals applying $\beta_{jk}$ and then the component of $\alpha_{kl}$, by naturality of the unit and the displayed cocycle identity. Thus $q_{j,l}$ after the inner transition equals $q_{j,k}$. For $j\le j'\le k$, $\beta_{j'k}\circ f_{j'k}^{-1}\beta_{jj'}=\beta_{jk}$, so these maps also obey the outer transitions. They induce $q:\varinjlim_j\varinjlim_{k\ge j}H_{j,k}\to L$. Conversely send $B_k=H_{k,k}$ into the iterated colimit by its two coprojections. The preceding identities make these maps a cocone on $B_k$, giving $r:L\to\varinjlim_j\varinjlim_{k\ge j}H_{j,k}$. We have $qr=\mathrm{id}$ on each $B_k$, since $\beta_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$. On each $H_{j,k}$, $rq$ equals its own coprojection: the outer transition from $j$ to $k$ sends it to $H_{k,k}$ by $\beta_{jk}$. The universal property of the two colimits gives $rq=\mathrm{id}$. This proves the required double-colimit identification without claiming that $\beta_{jk}$ itself is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A33, label lemma-descend-opens, proof: formal argument, expanded by its cocone universal properties

proof.text: Combining Steps 2, 3 and 4 gives $L\cong F(U)$. On $B_k$, the map is its unit into $G_k(U)$ followed by the sheaf-colimit coprojection into $F(U)$, because $r$ used $H_{k,k}$ and the pullback-sections isomorphism sends this diagonal term by precisely that unit. This is the canonical map in the statement. The transition $B_j\to B_k$ is pullback along $f_{jk}$ followed by $\beta_{jk}$, which by adjunction is exactly $\alpha_{jk,U_j}$. Every map constructed is additive, so the canonical bijection is an isomorphism of abelian groups.
